1	package factsync
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"context"
6		"encoding/json"
7		"errors"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"net"
11		"net/http"
12		"net/url"
13		"strings"
14		"time"
15	
16		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/apiurl"
17		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/httpx"
18		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/repoid"
19	)
20	
21	// HTTPServer is the real Server adapter: it drives entire-api's fact-set sync
22	// endpoints (internal/httpapi/brain_facts.go) over HTTP so the sync runner can talk to
23	// the hosted head. It is the production implementor of the Server seam that Sync/Resolve
24	// are written against (the tests use an in-memory fake with identical semantics).
25	//
26	// Wire contract (must stay in lockstep with brain_facts.go):
27	//
28	//	GET  {BaseURL}/api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts?branch=… → 200
29	//	     {found, ref, version, data(base64)}   (pull-gated)
30	//	POST {BaseURL}/api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts/advance  → 200
31	//	     {newRef, version, changed}           (push-gated)
32	//	     body {branch, oldRef, old_ref, data(base64)}
33	//	     412/409 → the head advanced concurrently (→ ErrConflict, re-read + re-merge)
34	//	     changed=false or unchanged:true → the merge changed nothing (→ ErrNoChange, converged)
35	//	     changed omitted with newRef==oldRef preserves legacy no-op compatibility
36	//
37	// Data crosses the wire base64-encoded: huma serializes a Go []byte as a base64 JSON
38	// string, and encoding/json here does the same on both sides, so the []byte fields match
39	// byte-for-byte. Authorization is a bearer token (the member's session/runner token).
40	type HTTPServer struct {
41		BaseURL string       // entire-api origin, e.g. https://api.entire.io (no trailing slash needed); must clear apiurl.Validate — https, or http only to loopback
42		Token   string       // bearer token; sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> when non-empty
43		Client  *http.Client // defaults to the bounded shared upload client when nil
44	}
45	
46	// syncRequestTimeout bounds one HTTP exchange, including a full fact-set upload.
47	// Tests may shorten it; the default matches the hosted publish upload budget.
48	var syncRequestTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
49	
50	func (h *HTTPServer) client() *http.Client {
51		if h.Client != nil {
52			return apiurl.WithoutRedirects(h.Client)
53		}
54		// The phase bounds (dial, TLS handshake, response header) come from the shared
55		// bounded transport; syncRequestTimeout is this caller's own end-to-end bound.
56		// A fresh Client per call is free — the transport, and so the connection pool,
57		// is shared.
58		return apiurl.WithoutRedirects(httpx.UploadClient(syncRequestTimeout))
59	}
60	
61	// syncOperationTimeout bounds the complete operation, including retries and
62	// response-body consumption. It must allow one syncRequestTimeout exchange.
63	// Tests may shorten it.
64	var syncOperationTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
65	
66	// transientDialRetries bounds how many times do() will redial after a local
67	// dial failure before giving up and returning it to the caller.
68	const transientDialRetries = 2
69	
70	// transientDialRetryDelay is the fixed pause between redial attempts. It only
71	// needs to outlast a momentary local resource crunch (see
72	// isTransientLocalDialError), not model network RTT or server load, so a flat
73	// short delay is enough — this is not a server-side backoff policy.
74	const transientDialRetryDelay = 20 * time.Millisecond
75	
76	// do retries transient local dial failures that occur before any request reaches
77	// the peer. Redirects are disabled, and GetBody rearms upload bodies. Other
78	// connectivity errors return immediately; retries share one operation deadline.
79	func (h *HTTPServer) do(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
80		// Retries and body consumption share the caller-bounded deadline.
81		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), syncOperationTimeout)
82		req = req.WithContext(ctx)
83	
84		var lastErr error
85		for attempt := 0; attempt <= transientDialRetries; attempt++ {
86			if attempt > 0 {
87				select {
88				case <-ctx.Done():
89					cancel()
90					return nil, ctx.Err()
91				case <-time.After(transientDialRetryDelay):
92				}
93				if req.GetBody != nil {
94					body, err := req.GetBody()
95					if err != nil {
96						cancel()
97						return nil, err
98					}
99					req.Body = body
100				}
101			}
102			resp, err := h.client().Do(req)
103			if err == nil {
104				// The deadline has to outlive do(): http.Client.Timeout covers the
105				// body read, so the operation budget must too, and cancelling here
106				// would break every caller that reads resp.Body afterwards. Hand the
107				// cancel to the body instead -- every factsync call site closes it.
108				resp.Body = &cancelOnCloseBody{ReadCloser: resp.Body, cancel: cancel}
109				return resp, nil
110			}
111			if !isTransientLocalDialError(err) {
112				cancel()
113				return nil, err
114			}
115			lastErr = err
116		}
117		cancel()
118		return nil, lastErr
119	}
120	
121	// cancelOnCloseBody releases the operation context when the caller closes the
122	// response body, which is the point the request is genuinely finished.
123	type cancelOnCloseBody struct {
124		io.ReadCloser
125		cancel context.CancelFunc
126	}
127	
128	func (b *cancelOnCloseBody) Close() error {
129		err := b.ReadCloser.Close()
130		b.cancel()
131		return err
132	}
133	
134	// isTransientLocalDialError reports whether err is a dial failure that never
135	// reached the peer and is known to self-resolve: local ephemeral-port/
136	// connection-table exhaustion. Matched by message rather than a syscall errno
137	// so this stays correct across platforms (Windows reports the same condition
138	// under a different errno) without a build-tagged file.
139	func isTransientLocalDialError(err error) bool {
140		var opErr *net.OpError
141		if !errors.As(err, &opErr) || opErr.Op != "dial" || opErr.Err == nil {
142			return false
143		}
144		return strings.Contains(opErr.Err.Error(), "assign requested address")
145	}
146	
147	// repoBasePath is the single point at which a repo id becomes part of a request
148	// target in this package. Every fact-set and proposal endpoint below is built on top
149	// of it, so the segment rule is applied once rather than once per endpoint.
150	//
151	// The id is interpolated by concatenation, so it has to be exactly one safe path
152	// segment: a "/", a "?" or a dot segment would otherwise re-address the request while
153	// newRequest attaches the member's bearer token to it. Escaping does not achieve
154	// that — "." and ".." are RFC 3986 unreserved, so url.PathEscape("..") == "..", and
155	//
156	//	/api/v1/repos/../brain/facts
157	//
158	// collapses at any normalizing hop to /api/v1/brain/facts, a route the caller never
159	// asked for. repoid.Validate states the rule instead; because it also requires the id
160	// to equal its own escaped form, the id is concatenated raw here — PathEscape would
161	// be a no-op and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe before.
162	//
163	// Returning an error (rather than a string) is deliberate: it forces every call site
164	// to refuse BEFORE http.NewRequest exists, so a rejected id costs zero egress.
165	func repoBasePath(repoID string) (string, error) {
166		if err := repoid.Validate(repoID); err != nil {
167			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: %w", err)
168		}
169		return "/api/v1/repos/" + repoID, nil
170	}
171	
172	// ErrBranchTooLong is returned when the caller's branch name exceeds the hosted
173	// fact-set API's cap. It is a distinct sentinel so a caller can tell a client-side
174	// refusal (nothing was sent; fix the branch) from a server rejection.
175	var ErrBranchTooLong = errors.New("factsync: branch name is too long for the hosted fact-set API")
176	
177	// maxBranchBytes is the hosted fact-set API's cap on a branch name, in BYTES as the
178	// server counts them (not runes — a multi-byte name is longer on the wire than it
179	// looks on screen).
180	//
181	// This is the ONE server cap this client mirrors, and it is worth saying why, because
182	// mirroring a server-owned number is normally a bug waiting to happen: if the hosted
183	// cap is raised, a client that hardcoded the old one refuses branches the server would
184	// now accept, and no amount of error-body surfacing helps because the request is never
185	// made. Two things make this cap the exception:
186	//
187	//   - The round trip it saves is expensive and pointless. The branch is known before
188	//     a socket is opened, and the request that would learn the limit carries the
189	//     member's bearer token and, on Advance/Resolve, the member's whole fact set — a
190	//     multi-megabyte upload posted only to be told the branch name was too long.
191	//   - The number is not close to anything real. Git states no length limit of its own
192	//     on a ref name — the effective one is the filesystem's — and a branch anywhere
193	//     near 512 bytes is pathological rather than merely long, so nothing a member
194	//     would plausibly name a branch sits near this value.
195	//
196	// The residual risk is stated rather than hidden: if the hosted cap is RAISED, this
197	// client refuses a branch the server would now accept, and it cannot detect that on
198	// its own, because the request it would have learned from is the one it declined to
199	// make. Raising this constant is then the fix, and it is one line. That risk is
200	// accepted only because the value is far outside the range of real branch names; it is
201	// why no other server-owned cap is mirrored here.
202	//
203	// The other caps the hosted API grew at the same time are deliberately NOT mirrored:
204	// the artifact count and the manifest reference count on the publish path, and
205	// whatever the hosted MCP query surface applies to its own branch argument. The client
206	// has no independent basis for those numbers (unlike the publish body-size ceiling,
207	// which it must project anyway to avoid building a multi-GB buffer), and the hosted
208	// MCP branch is server-defaulted, so a guessed constant there would refuse requests
209	// the server accepts. Those are surfaced from the server's own error body instead —
210	// see internal/cli/publish.go and internal/hostedbrain/client.go.
211	const maxBranchBytes = 512
212	
213	// validateBranch refuses a branch the hosted API is known to reject, before the
214	// request exists.
215	func validateBranch(branch string) error {
216		if len(branch) > maxBranchBytes {
217			return fmt.Errorf("%w: branch is %d bytes, limit is %d", ErrBranchTooLong, len(branch), maxBranchBytes)
218		}
219		return nil
220	}
221	
222	// detail renders the server's objection with this client's own bearer token removed.
223	// Every non-2xx render on the fact-set and proposal surfaces goes through here, so
224	// the redaction is applied once rather than at each of the ten call sites. See
225	// httpx.Redact for why an echoed token has to be stripped even though the peer that
226	// echoed it already had it.
227	func (h *HTTPServer) detail(resp *http.Response) string {
228		return httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorSuffix(resp), h.Token)
229	}
230	
231	// conflict renders a 412/409 as ErrConflict, carrying whatever the server said about
232	// the head that moved.
233	//
234	// The SENTINEL is the contract: Sync and the proposal loops re-read and re-merge on
235	// errors.Is(err, ErrConflict), so a CAS loss must keep matching it no matter how the
236	// message grows. fmt.Errorf with %w preserves that; a plain formatted error would
237	// silently turn a converging retry into a failed sync. When the server said nothing
238	// the bare sentinel is returned unchanged, so a quiet 412 reads exactly as it did
239	// before this file learned to read bodies.
240	func (h *HTTPServer) conflict(resp *http.Response) error {
241		if detail := httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorDetail(resp), h.Token); detail != "" {
242			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrConflict, detail)
243		}
244		return ErrConflict
245	}
246	
247	// requestTarget is the single chokepoint for the two caller-supplied values that
248	// decide whether a fact-set request can possibly succeed: the repo id, which must be
249	// exactly one safe path segment (repoBasePath), and the branch, which must be within
250	// the hosted cap. Both are checked before http.NewRequest exists, so a request that
251	// cannot succeed costs zero egress.
252	func requestTarget(repoID, branch string) (string, error) {
253		// Repo id first: it is the check that keeps the request on the route the caller
254		// asked for, so when both values are bad that is the one worth reporting.
255		base, err := repoBasePath(repoID)
256		if err != nil {
257			return "", err
258		}
259		if err := validateBranch(branch); err != nil {
260			return "", err
261		}
262		return base, nil
263	}
264	
265	func (h *HTTPServer) newRequest(ctx context.Context, method, path string, body io.Reader) (*http.Request, error) {
266		// Scheme floor (apiurl.Validate) at the single request chokepoint of both the
267		// fact-set and the proposal-queue surfaces: the bearer token below and the
268		// fact-set blob above it must never be built into a plaintext request to a
269		// non-loopback host. Every construction path lands here, so a caller that
270		// bypassed the CLI's own check is still covered.
271		base, err := apiurl.Validate(h.BaseURL)
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil, fmt.Errorf("factsync: %w", err)
274		}
275		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, base+path, body)
276		if err != nil {
277			return nil, err
278		}
279		if h.Token != "" {
280			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+h.Token)
281		}
282		if body != nil {
283			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
284		}
285		return req, nil
286	}
287	
288	// Current reads the branch's fact-set head. A 200 with found=false (no head yet) returns
289	// found=false and nil plaintext; the data field is base64-decoded by encoding/json into
290	// the []byte. Any non-200 is an error (the runner cannot merge against an unknown state).
291	func (h *HTTPServer) Current(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (string, []byte, bool, error) {
292		ref, plaintext, _, found, err := h.CurrentWithAuthors(ctx, repoID, branch)
293		return ref, plaintext, found, err
294	}
295	
296	// CurrentWithAuthors is Current plus the additive per-fact attribution map the
297	// hosted server stamps on the GET response (fact id → display handle). A server
298	// without the field yields a nil map — the sync contract is unchanged.
299	func (h *HTTPServer) CurrentWithAuthors(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (string, []byte, map[string]string, bool, error) {
300		base, err := requestTarget(repoID, branch)
301		if err != nil {
302			return "", nil, nil, false, err
303		}
304		path := base + "/brain/facts?branch=" + url.QueryEscape(branch)
305		req, err := h.newRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil)
306		if err != nil {
307			return "", nil, nil, false, err
308		}
309		resp, err := h.do(req)
310		if err != nil {
311			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: GET fact-set head %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
312		}
313		defer resp.Body.Close()
314		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
315			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: GET fact-set head %s/%s: unexpected status %s%s", repoID, branch, resp.Status, h.detail(resp))
316		}
317		var out struct {
318			Found   bool              `json:"found"`
319			Ref     string            `json:"ref"`
320			Version int64             `json:"version"`
321			Data    []byte            `json:"data"`
322			Authors map[string]string `json:"authors"`
323		}
324		if err := httpx.DecodeJSONBody(resp, &out); err != nil {
325			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode fact-set head %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
326		}
327		if !out.Found {
328			return "", nil, nil, false, nil
329		}
330		return out.Ref, out.Data, out.Authors, true, nil
331	}
332	
333	// Advance compare-and-swaps the head onto plaintext, mapping the endpoint's outcomes to
334	// the Server contract: 200 with changed → the new ref; 200 with changed=false
335	// or unchanged:true → ErrNoChange; 412/409 → ErrConflict. Any other status is
336	// an error (a 400 empty-data, 404 unknown repo, 503 unconfigured, or 5xx —
337	// none of which the runner should paper over). The duplicated ref spellings
338	// keep mixed-version entire-api / entire-brain rollouts compatible.
339	func (h *HTTPServer) Advance(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch, oldRef string, plaintext []byte) (string, error) {
340		base, err := requestTarget(repoID, branch)
341		if err != nil {
342			return "", err
343		}
344		reqBody := struct {
345			Branch       string `json:"branch"`
346			OldRef       string `json:"oldRef"`
347			OldRefLegacy string `json:"old_ref"`
348			Data         []byte `json:"data"`
349		}{Branch: branch, OldRef: oldRef, OldRefLegacy: oldRef, Data: plaintext}
350		buf, err := json.Marshal(reqBody)
351		if err != nil {
352			return "", err
353		}
354	
355		path := base + "/brain/facts/advance"
356		req, err := h.newRequest(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, bytes.NewReader(buf))
357		if err != nil {
358			return "", err
359		}
360		resp, err := h.do(req)
361		if err != nil {
362			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: POST advance %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
363		}
364		defer resp.Body.Close()
365	
366		switch resp.StatusCode {
367		case http.StatusOK:
368			var out struct {
369				NewRef          string `json:"newRef"`
370				NewRefLegacy    string `json:"new_ref"`
371				Version         int64  `json:"version"`
372				Changed         *bool  `json:"changed"`
373				UnchangedLegacy *bool  `json:"unchanged"`
374			}
375			if err := httpx.DecodeJSONBody(resp, &out); err != nil {
376				return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode advance %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
377			}
378			if out.Changed != nil && !*out.Changed {
379				return "", ErrNoChange
380			}
381			if out.UnchangedLegacy != nil && *out.UnchangedLegacy {
382				return "", ErrNoChange
383			}
384			newRef := out.NewRef
385			if newRef == "" {
386				newRef = out.NewRefLegacy
387			}
388			if out.Changed == nil && out.UnchangedLegacy == nil && oldRef != "" && newRef == oldRef {
389				return "", ErrNoChange
390			}
391			if newRef == "" {
392				return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode advance %s/%s: missing new ref", repoID, branch)
393			}
394			return newRef, nil
395		case http.StatusPreconditionFailed, http.StatusConflict:
396			// The sentinel is the contract (sync.go re-reads and re-merges on
397			// errors.Is(err, ErrConflict)); the server's account of WHICH head moved is
398			// additive, and only when it said something.
399			return "", h.conflict(resp)
400		default:
401			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: POST advance %s/%s: unexpected status %s%s", repoID, branch, resp.Status, h.detail(resp))
402		}
403	}

1	# Repairing invalid proposal IDs
2	
3	Hosted proposal listing and resolution reject IDs that do not match the decision
4	they name. A malformed entry blocks the branch's normal queue operations rather
5	than allowing an agent to resolve a substituted decision.
6	
7	Use the explicit repair command to inspect the rejected entries without resolving
8	proposals or changing facts. The same hosted opt-in, no-egress, credentials, repo,
9	and branch settings as other `facts proposals` commands apply.
10	
11	```sh
12	entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --json
13	```
14	
15	Review the returned `invalid` entries and save the output for diagnosis. To remove
16	only those malformed entries, copy the exact `ref` from that preview:
17	
18	```sh
19	entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --apply --if-ref '<preview ref>'
20	```

# Repairing invalid proposal IDs

Hosted proposal listing and resolution reject IDs that do not match the decision
they name. A malformed entry blocks the branch's normal queue operations rather
than allowing an agent to resolve a substituted decision.

Use the explicit repair command to inspect the rejected entries without resolving
proposals or changing facts. The same hosted opt-in, no-egress, credentials, repo,
and branch settings as other `facts proposals` commands apply.

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --json
```

Review the returned `invalid` entries and save the output for diagnosis. To remove
only those malformed entries, copy the exact `ref` from that preview:

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --apply --if-ref '<preview ref>'
```

The command preserves valid proposals and never writes the shared fact head or
local fact store. Both the preview ref check and the server's compare-and-swap
must match. If the queue changed, preview it again; repair does not automatically
retry against entries that were not in the reviewed snapshot. Normal proposal
listing and resolution keep their identity checks; repair is an explicit
maintenance operation, not a verification bypass.

Missing IDs from older servers are derived as usual and are not removed. This
command repairs proposal ID/content mismatches only. It does not authenticate
provenance, repair malformed JSON, or repair a shared fact-set head.

1	// Package factsync is the runner-side read-merge-CAS loop that syncs a member's
2	// durable facts into the hosted, shared fact-set head. It is where the two P1.M2
3	// halves meet: the deterministic merge engine (factmerge) and the hosted
4	// atomic head (entire-api's FactSetStore, reached here through the Server seam).
5	//
6	// Per ADR-P1-E the MERGE runs on the runner (this package), not in the API server:
7	// the server only stores encrypted blobs and compare-and-swaps the branch head, so
8	// it never needs the cgo/SQLite-heavy brain merge core. Sync pulls the current head
9	// in plaintext, keep-both promotes the member's local facts into it via factmerge,
10	// and pushes the result back under CAS — retrying on a losing swap.
11	package factsync
12	
13	import (
14		"bytes"
15		"context"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"time"
19	
20		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge"
21	)
22	
23	// ErrConflict is what a Server.Advance returns when the head moved under it (a
24	// concurrent member advanced first) — the signal for Sync to re-read and re-merge.
25	var ErrConflict = errors.New("factsync: fact-set head changed (CAS conflict)")
26	
27	// ErrNoChange is what a Server.Advance returns when the merged blob is byte-identical
28	// to the current head — the member's facts were all already present. Sync treats it as
29	// "converged, nothing to publish", not an error.
30	var ErrNoChange = errors.New("factsync: fact-set unchanged by merge")
31	
32	// ErrExhausted is returned when Sync cannot land its merge within maxAttempts CAS
33	// tries — sustained contention the caller should retry later or escalate.
34	var ErrExhausted = errors.New("factsync: exceeded CAS retries")
35	
36	// maxAttempts bounds the read-merge-CAS loop so pathological contention fails loudly
37	// instead of spinning forever.
38	const maxAttempts = 32
39	
40	// Server is the runner's view of the hosted fact-set head (entire-api's FactSetStore
41	// over HTTP). Current returns the branch head's content ref and the DECRYPTED facts
42	// blob (found=false, nil blob when the branch has no head yet — merge into empty).
43	// Advance seals+stores the merged plaintext and compare-and-swaps the head from oldRef
44	// onto its content ref, returning ErrConflict on a losing swap and ErrNoChange when the
45	// merge produced exactly the current content.
46	type Server interface {
47		Current(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (ref string, plaintext []byte, found bool, err error)
48		Advance(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch, oldRef string, plaintext []byte) (newRef string, err error)
49	}
50	
51	// Result reports the outcome of a Sync: whether the head advanced (Published), the new
52	// content ref, how many CAS attempts it took, and any review Proposals the keep-both
53	// merge queued (cross-member conflicts a human must resolve — the M2.4 surface).
54	type Result struct {
55		Published bool
56		NewRef    string
57		Attempts  int
58		Proposals []factmerge.Proposal
59	
60		// Facts is the fact set this sync settled on: the merged content when the CAS
61		// won, or the head as read when it converged with no change. The runner already
62		// computed it, so a caller needing the post-sync head (to check which proposals
63		// are still live, or to mirror settlements into local facts) can use this
64		// instead of issuing another Current — one fewer network round-trip per sync.
65		Facts []factmerge.Record
66	}
67	
68	// Sync runs the read-merge-CAS loop: pull the head, keep-both promote local into it via
69	// factmerge, push under CAS, retry on ErrConflict. `now` is injected for determinism.
70	// memberID identifies the syncing member; it is stamped onto every review Proposal the
71	// merge raises (ProposedBy) so a cross-member conflict is attributable and routable.
72	// A keep-both merge NEVER silently drops a member's fact (ADR-P1-G): identical facts
73	// (same content id) union their provenance; genuine conflicts are kept and queued as
74	// routed Proposals in the Result (resolve them with Resolve).
75	func Sync(ctx context.Context, srv Server, repoID, branch, memberID string, local []factmerge.Record, now time.Time) (Result, error) {
76		if memberID == "" {
77			// A blank memberID would stamp ProposedBy="" (dropped by omitempty), making a
78			// cross-member proposal indistinguishable from a local one — routing lost. Reject.
79			return Result{}, errors.New("factsync: memberID is required (proposal routing)")
80		}
81		// Redact local-only provenance coordinates before these facts leave for the shared
82		// head — no member's local filesystem path leaks cross-member (opaque ids are kept,
83		// so provenance still unions). Copies; the caller's local facts are not mutated.
84		local = SanitizeForEgress(local)
85		// Verify this member's own facts BEFORE publishing them. The head check below
86		// fails closed, so one malformed record reaching the shared head would break
87		// every other member's sync — a failure the member that produced it should
88		// take, and take here, rather than exporting it.
89		if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(local); err != nil {
90			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("factsync: local fact set for %s/%s is not publishable: %w", repoID, branch, err)
91		}
92		for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ {
93			ref, plaintext, found, err := srv.Current(ctx, repoID, branch)
94			if err != nil {
95				return Result{}, err
96			}
97			var head []factmerge.Record
98			if found && len(plaintext) > 0 {
99				head, err = factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(plaintext))
100				if err != nil {
101					return Result{}, err
102				}
103				// The head is written by every member with push access, so nothing about
104				// it is authenticated by having arrived over the transport. Re-derive each
105				// record's content id before merging: without this, a record carrying
106				// ANOTHER member's id with attacker-chosen text makes Promote's id match
107				// read as "already present, union the provenance", silently discarding the
108				// victim's real statement and keeping the forgery — with the victim's own
109				// anchors attached to it. Fail closed rather than merge a head one record
110				// of which is provably not what it claims to be.
111				if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(head); err != nil {
112					return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("factsync: shared fact-set head for %s/%s is not trustworthy: %w", repoID, branch, err)
113				}
114			}
115	
116			// Cross-member merge is structurally cross-branch promote: the member's local
117			// facts are the "source" promoted (keep-both) into the current head "target".
118			merged, proposals, _ := factmerge.Promote(local, head, "keep-both", branch, now)
119			// Promote only carries ACTIVE source facts, so a member's RETIREMENTS
120			// (a `facts retract`, or a supersede they applied in review) never reach
121			// the head on their own: the head keeps listing the statement as active,
122			// Advance sees byte-identical content and reports "no change", and every
123			// other member goes on reading a statement its owner declared false.
124			// Carry them over explicitly. Nothing is deleted — the record and its
125			// provenance stay and only the status is retired — so the keep-both
126			// guarantee (ADR-P1-G) holds.
127			merged = applyLocalRetirements(local, merged, now)
128			// Stamp routing: every conflict this member's sync raised is attributed to it.
129			for i := range proposals {
130				proposals[i].ProposedBy = memberID
131			}
132	
133			var buf bytes.Buffer
134			if err := factmerge.WriteNDJSON(&buf, merged); err != nil {
135				return Result{}, err
136			}
137			if buf.Len() == 0 {
138				// The merge produced an EMPTY fact-set (an empty head and no active local
139				// facts to promote). There is nothing to publish — a head always points at
140				// content, and Advance rejects empty plaintext — so report converged rather
141				// than push an empty blob. (A non-empty head can never merge to empty: promote
142				// only grows the target.)
143				return Result{Published: false, NewRef: ref, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
144			}
145	
146			newRef, err := srv.Advance(ctx, repoID, branch, ref, buf.Bytes())
147			switch {
148			case err == nil:
149				return Result{Published: true, NewRef: newRef, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
150			case errors.Is(err, ErrNoChange):
151				return Result{Published: false, NewRef: ref, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
152			case errors.Is(err, ErrConflict):
153				continue // a concurrent member advanced first — re-read the newer head and re-merge
154			default:
155				return Result{}, err
156			}
157		}
158		return Result{}, ErrExhausted
159	}
160	
161	// applyLocalRetirements folds a member's non-active local facts onto the merged
162	// set: a record the shared head still lists as active is retired to the status
163	// its owner gave it, carrying the SupersededBy pointer. It only ever moves a
164	// fact from active to retracted/superseded — it never revives one and never
165	// removes one — so the merge stays monotone and a second sync of the same local
166	// state is a no-op.
167	func applyLocalRetirements(local, merged []factmerge.Record, now time.Time) []factmerge.Record {
168		for _, l := range local {
169			if l.Status != factmerge.StatusRetracted && l.Status != factmerge.StatusSuperseded {
170				continue
171			}
172			i := factmerge.IndexOf(merged, l.ID)
173			if i < 0 || merged[i].Status != factmerge.StatusActive {
174				continue
175			}
176			merged[i].Status = l.Status
177			merged[i].SupersededBy = l.SupersededBy
178			merged[i].UpdatedAt = now
179		}
180		return merged
181	}

I'm scoping COR-2234: for connected repos, plain `memories sync` should default to the per-fact hosted sync path when no explicit backend is set, the repo is connected and not opted out, and egress is allowed—reusing the hostedFactsSyncAndPull logic but surfacing real errors instead of silently succeeding like the background sync does.

I'm thinking through the refactor: rather than letting the manual sync swallow failures like the background wrapper does, I want to split hostedFactsSyncAndPull into a core that returns detailed outcomes and errors, keeping a never-fails wrapper around it for background callers while the manual CLI path propagates failures properly. I also need to preserve explicit backend overrides (local-gitmeta/http), leave unconnected-repo behavior unchanged for now, and update the help text to describe the new default and connectedness behavior.

Since gates (connection checks) differ between manual and background callers, I'm keeping that logic in the wrapper rather than the shared core. For the push step specifically, I'm reworking pushHostedFacts to return counts and an error instead of just printing — background callers can still catch that error and degrade gracefully to pull-only, while the manual command treats a push failure as a real, honest failure.

For the pull step and manifest refresh, I'm weighing whether a manifest error should fail the whole sync or just surface as a warning — the actual fact sync (push+pull) succeeding is distinct from the manifest being stale, and I don't think treating manifest staleness as a sync failure would violate the "honest exit codes" precedent, since the manifest just gets refreshed on the next operation anyway.

Now I'm looking at how to connect the manual `--memories-backend=http` path for COR-2235 so it routes through the per-fact wire protocol instead of the CAS flow — this means restructuring runFactsSync to first decide whether the path is per-fact hosted (default when connected, or explicit http) versus local CAS, and then removing the CAS client components entirely: the HTTPServer sync methods, the proposal-queue plumbing, and related hosted branch code.

But I'm pausing to check scope — removing the `memories proposals` command would also drop a documented user-facing feature and the repair workflow described in the proposal-queue-repair doc, so I need to be careful about whether the ticket actually wants that fully deleted or just quarantined.

Since the proposals queue is only fed by CAS-wire syncs, stopping manual sync publishing would starve it, but existing hosted queues might still have open proposals users need to settle — so I'm weighing whether to cut the command and publishing path now with server endpoints staying temporarily for old clients, versus keeping the command alive just long enough to let people clear out leftovers. I'm also noting that per-fact storage now keeps conflicting facts side by side and resolves them asynchronously, so new conflicts won't even generate hosted proposals going forward.

For this repo, I'm mapping out the specific deletions needed: the CAS client methods, httpproposals client methods, the hosted resolve logic in factsync/review, the hostedbrain client's proposal methods, the proposals command file, and the publishing step in facts sync.

Also the hosted proposal publishing block itself becomes dead code once no hosted CAS server exists (since local gitmeta doesn't implement the ProposalTransport interface), along with the shared proposal ledger and hosted reconciliation logic. I need to be careful though — the local review queue and persistFactsSyncProposals should stay, since I need to verify whether local gitmeta sync still raises proposals on cross-member conflicts or whether that's strictly a per-machine, non-conflicting scenario.

I should keep factsync.Sync and its Server seam for local gitmeta along with ErrConflict, but delete or retire the proposal-queue-repair doc and check other docs referencing the old proposal/HTTP backend. There's also a writeHostedFactsBinding call in runFactsSync tied to HTTPServer that needs to move to the per-fact path, while the blind spot detection logic stays unchanged since it keys off the binding marker rather than the backend type. COR-2236 is still blocked on a decision, so I'll need to flag that for Evis at the end.

For process, I'm weighing whether to use AskUserQuestion now versus waiting until I finish 2234 and 2235 first, commit, and possibly open a PR before raising the 2236 question. I'm also unsure whether to open separate PRs per sub-issue or bundle 2234+2235 into one PR with separate commits, since the tickets imply separate branches but we're working in a single workspace.

I think one PR covering both 2234 and 2235, with the 2236 decision left pending, is the cleanest approach, and I need to remember to pull the latest main before opening any PR — even though I'm on a branch Conductor already created, so I should fetch origin main first.

Before diving in, I still need to do more recon: identify all callers of the never-fails sync wrapper (daemon tick, hook command, connect command), figure out which factsync files are CAS/hosted-only versus local, check the hosted brain client's proposal methods, review MCP tool descriptions and status/setup output referencing sync backends, and look at the relevant test files and the legacy flag alias handling.

I also need to think through the environment variable backend setting — the `http` value needs to keep meaning "hosted sync" even though the underlying mechanism shifts to per-fact rather than proposal-based. Per the compatibility constraints, existing `--memories-backend` values shouldn't silently change meaning, so I'm weighing whether keeping `http` accepted but rewiring it to the per-fact path (with a documented note) counts as an acceptable semantic preservation or a silent behavior change that needs a deprecation warning instead.

I'll settle on keeping the mapping but printing a one-time notice that http now uses the per-fact wire and the proposals queue is retired, and confirm that explicit http with manual repo-id/api-url/token still resolves correctly through resolveManualHostedTarget, with pullHostedFacts deriving member identity from the token's JWT claim. Next I want to gather more context by reading through httpproposals.go, review.go, proposals.go, proposal_repair.go, the hosted brain client, and searching for other backend references across MCP, status, and docs.

content.thinking:
I'm locating the MCP sync logic in internal/cli/mcp*.go and realizing this requires a larger multi-file change. I'm sketching a plan for COR-2234, starting with how runFactsSync should resolve the backend name—honoring explicit flag/env values like "local-gitmeta" for local CAS.

I'm also working out edge cases: when the repo is connected but no-egress is set, hosted sync should be silently suppressed and fall back to local-gitmeta with a note, while explicit http plus no-egress should still error. For hosted manual sync, I'm planning a new function that pushes then pulls facts, writes a sync marker, and prints a summary, treating manifest errors as warnings but push/pull failures as hard errors—refactoring the existing push/pull helpers to separate counting logic from printing so the background wrapper can degrade gracefully.

I'm now deciding that for the manual sync path, unlike the background sync which degrades to pull-only on push failure, I should run both push and pull regardless of errors, collect any failures, report them clearly, and exit nonzero if either failed—since that's more honest and still gets users their teammates' memories.

For the output format, I want a line summarizing what synced on which branch via the hosted per-fact wire, including push counts (added/changed/unchanged) and pull counts (feed facts received/kept), with JSON output supported too via the existing jsonOut flag. I also need to update the help text to document that the default backend depends on connectedness, with hosted being per-fact wire sync, local-gitmeta for unconnected cases, and no-egress suppression behavior.

Moving to COR-2235, retiring the CAS client: the http backend should route through manual per-fact sync via resolveManualHostedTarget, keeping the "hosted" semantics intact while updating help text to note that proposals are no longer published.

Now I need to strip out the proposal transport machinery from facts_sync_cmd.go — things like reading shared fact heads, checking if proposals are still open, settled-hosted-as-accept logic, reconciling the local proposal queue, publishing raised proposals, and the shared ledger helpers. But I'm realizing facts_admin_cmd.go depends on loadSharedProposalLedger to block settling shared proposals locally during memory review, so if the hosted queue is retired, that gating logic becomes a dead end since the command it points users to no longer exists — meaning local review should just settle everything unconditionally. I'm also considering what happens to proposals that were previously shared on the now-retired hosted queue.

Teammates on older clients could still settle those via the old path, so the deprecation approach is simply that new clients ignore the shared ledger and hosted queue entirely and settle locally, consistent with keeping per-fact conflicts side by side and deferring resolution to the async pipeline. I'm tracing applySettlementLocally's usage back to facts_proposals_cmd and reconcileLocalProposalQueue, both slated for deletion, so that function goes too — along with facts_proposals_cmd.go, hostedbrain/proposals.go, and the factsync httpproposals, proposals, and proposal_repair files, while I check whether review.go's Resolve/Decision types are used anywhere beyond facts_proposals_cmd.

It looks like local review actually wraps factmerge directly via facts_aliases.go, so review.go can likely be deleted too, pending a check of tests and other Decision usages. I'm also tracking ProposalID's remaining references in the deleted facts_sync ledger, the facts_admin shared-ledger gate being removed, and a reconcile.go comment — if those all go, ProposalID can be removed from proposals.go as well, though I'll let the compiler catch any stragglers. For HTTPServer, I'm planning to strip Current/CurrentWithAuthors/Advance from httpserver.go while keeping the core struct and request helpers that perfact.go still relies on.

The Sync/Server seam stays intact for gitmeta, and factsync.Sync now only has one caller through runFactsSync, so that's straightforward. The bigger challenge is the test suite — many factsync tests cover CAS-related methods across body_limit, error_body, httpserver, repoid_segment, token_redaction, wire_fuzz, proposals, review, and authors tests, so I'll need substantial surgery to retarget these toward the perfact surface, especially tests exercising Advance that should shift to UpsertFacts/FactsFeedPage. Finally, I need to delete docs/proposal-queue-repair.md and update any references to it.

Since the shared-ledger writes went through ProposalTransport only, and the local gitmeta backend never implemented that interface, the ledger was effectively hosted-path-only — so removing it is consistent with keeping gitmeta as-is pending COR-2236. On the CLI side, I need to check the memories review error message referencing 'memories proposals' and remove that gate, plus check blind_spot references and the reconcile.go comment about ProposalID derivation. I should also check hostedbrain.Client files since proposals.go there was deleted, and verify whether factsyncServer() is only used for proposals.

For server endpoints, I'm deciding these stay for a deprecation window to support older CLIs, then get versioned off after a stable release — I'll note that in Linear. I also need to trace writeHostedFactsBinding (writes per-fact paths after push+pull succeed), the member identity lookup via jwtSubClaim for per-fact pull filtering (which works the same for manual --token targets), and hostedFeedDirForKey for the feed cache directory. I'm also noting that pullHostedFacts invalidates its cache when the repo ID or base URL changes, meaning manual explicit targets to a different host should work correctly.

Now I'm sketching the difference between the manual path and hostedFactsSyncAndPull — it mainly comes down to gates, error handling, and where the target originates. I'm designing a core function that performs the per-fact sync and returns honest stats plus separate push/pull errors, with a background wrapper that swallows failures for logging purposes and a manual wrapper that surfaces them directly. Restructuring hosted_sync.go around this...

I need to track pushed success separately from the skipped-records warning, and figure out where manual publishing lives relative to background sync. For the manual path, I think I can reuse resolveManualHostedTarget even for a connected repo with no explicit flags, since the consent gate, repo ID, and base URL would all resolve naturally from the binding with a minted token.

On the connected default case, environment overrides like ENTIRE_REPO_ID should still apply, consistent with the existing manual-http semantics, so I'll keep one unified resolution path rather than branching. If minting fails on a connected repo, that should be an honest failure rather than silently falling back to local storage, matching the COR-2234 requirement for honest exit codes. I'll add a small helper to determine "connected" status based on binding presence and opt-out state.

For no-egress scenarios without an explicit backend, I'll default to local-gitmeta and print a note to stderr when connected, explaining that the no-egress setting forced local storage — staying honest about the behavior. For unconnected repos with no backend specified, local-gitmeta remains the current default pending COR-2236.

For the JSON output format, I'm sketching a simple payload structure for manual hosted syncs covering branch, backend, push counts by status, and skipped counts.

On backend labeling, I'm leaning toward "hosted (url)" over the older "http (url)" phrasing, accepting this as a breaking JSON shape change worth noting in the PR since things are still pre-stable. For deprecation, `--memories-backend=http` isn't being removed, just conceptually renamed, so I don't think it needs a warning — the help text can just document the mapping to "hosted" silently.

On flag naming, I'll keep `local-gitmeta` and `http` as the actual accepted values unchanged to minimize surface area, letting a later ticket (COR-2236) revisit naming more thoroughly — just the backend logic behind `http` and the default resolution shift now.

                 (<cache>/brain/<repo-key>/gitmeta.git); fully local, no network,
                 entiredb, or Postgres. Default on unconnected repos.
  http           the hosted backend, explicitly. Default on connected repos.
                 Target resolves flag > env > connected binding:
                 --api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL, --repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID,
                 --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the binding
                 supplies the target and the token is minted automatically.`,
		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			return runFactsSync(cmd, opts, syncOpts)
		},
	}
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&syncOpts.branch, "branch", "", "Branch to sync (default: current branch)")
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&syncOpts.backend, "memories-backend", "", "Memory-set backend: local-gitmeta or http (default: http on a connected repo, else local-gitmeta)")

content.content:
sync exchanges this branch's local memories with the shared memory set.

The default backend depends on connectedness. On a repo connected to Brainstore
('entire brain connect'), a plain sync uses the hosted per-fact wire: push this
branch's memories, pull the team's delta feed — the same exchange the background
sync runs, except failures fail the command instead of degrading silently. On an
unconnected repo, a plain sync uses the fully local git-meta store and never
leaves the machine. ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS (or its deprecated alias
ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY) suppresses hosted sync regardless of defaults and
flags, falling back to the local store.

Backends (--memories-backend, or ENTIRE_BRAIN_FACTS_BACKEND):
  local-gitmeta  a bare, on-disk git-meta store under the brain cache
                 (<cache>/brain/<repo-key>/gitmeta.git); fully local, no network,
                 entiredb, or Postgres. Default on unconnected repos.
  http           the hosted per-fact wire, explicitly. Default on connected
                 repos. Target resolves flag > env > connected binding:
                 --api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL, --repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID,
                 --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the binding
                 supplies the target and the token is minted automatically.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories sync [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string            Entire API base URL for the http backend, https:// (overrides ENTIRE_API_URL)
      --branch string             Branch to sync (default: current branch)
  -h, --help                      help for sync
      --json                      Emit the sync result as JSON
      --member string             Member identity stamped on queued review proposals (default: git user.email)
      --memories-backend string   Memory-set backend: local-gitmeta or http (default: http on a connected repo, else local-gitmeta)
      --repo-id string            Target repo id for the http backend (overrides ENTIRE_REPO_ID)
      --token string              Entire API bearer token for the http backend (overrides ENTIRE_API_TOKEN)

aiTitle: Unify entire-brain memory sync on per-fact wire

content.thinking:
Wait, that run wasn't just a demonstration — it actually executed a real local gitmeta sync of 1546 facts and queued 1365 conflicts into this repo's review queue, a genuine side effect on the user's local brain state. The review queue now durably holds 1365 low-confidence supersede proposals from the keep-both merge of the branch store, which it didn't have before.

This matters because `memories review` surfaces these, and the pending-review guard might warn about them, polluting the local queue even though this is a pre-existing code path that would've behaved the same way before my changes. I'm now considering whether I can undo this — rejecting all proposals would mutate facts, which feels risky since most candidates are already active, so restoring the queue file to its likely-empty prior state seems safer, while the advanced gitmeta head is probably harmless cache state.

I'm weighing whether to delete the proposals file outright since every entry traces to this run with ProposedBy=evis@entire.io, but hand-editing brain state feels risky even if it's reverting my own side effect — there's no way to be sure no legitimate prior entries exist with that same attribution. The safest path might just be leaving the queue as-is and explaining to Evis that these proposals are a legitimate reflection of the divergence between their branch store and gitmeta head.

Actually, this exposes a deeper design issue: when a repo is connected but NO_EGRESS is set and no backend is explicit, silently falling back to a full local-gitmeta sync against a stale head seems worse than doing nothing, since it can spray out hundreds of spurious conflict proposals. I'm now considering whether the fallback behavior should instead be a no-op with a warning rather than running that stale sync automatically.

I think the better option is: connected plus NO_EGRESS should just print a note and exit cleanly without doing anything, since hosted sync is suppressed and local-only sync should require an explicit flag. Unify memory sync on the per-fact wire; retire the CAS client and hosted proposals queue

COR-2234: on a connected repo, plain `memories sync` now syncs over the
hosted per-fact wire (batch upsert + delta feed) by default — connect is
the consent moment, reconciling the hosted default with ADR-P1-A
(reverses COR-2211). Failures fail the command and name the failed half
(COR-2202 precedent). Under ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS a connected repo's
plain sync is skipped loudly instead of merging against the stale local
git-meta head, which would re-raise every deferred per-fact conflict
into the local review queue. Unconnected repos keep the local-gitmeta
default pending COR-2236.

COR-2235: --memories-backend=http drives the same per-fact exchange, so
one hosted wire remains. Removed: the branch-head CAS client
(HTTPServer.Current/CurrentWithAuthors/Advance), the hosted proposals
queue client and `memories proposals` command (incl. repair and
docs/proposal-queue-repair.md), the shared-proposal ledger, sync-time
proposal publishing/reconciliation, and the `memories review` interlock
that deferred shared proposals to the hosted queue. The factsync Server
CAS seam stays — the local git-meta backend is now its only implementor.

Server-side impact check: current entire-api routes only
/repos/{id}/brain/facts (upsert + feed) through the gateway to
brainstore; the advance/proposals endpoints no longer exist server-side,
so this client was their last consumer and no deprecation window is
needed.

Compat: --memories-backend/ENTIRE_BRAIN_FACTS_BACKEND values keep their
meaning (local-gitmeta unchanged; http still means hosted). The sync
--json payload for hosted runs now reports upsert counts and feed totals
instead of CAS head/proposal fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1 && git status --short | head -3
